events.title: Boston Massacre
events.description: British soldiers fired into a crowd of colonists on King Street in Boston, killing five people after tensions over the occupation of the city and taxation escalated.
events.significance: The incident inflamed anti-British sentiment in the American colonies and became a rallying point in the lead-up to the American Revolution.

events.title: Death of Joseph Stalin
events.description: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died at his dacha near Moscow after suffering a stroke, ending nearly three decades of absolute rule over the Soviet Union.
events.significance: His death triggered a power struggle and led to de-Stalinization under Nikita Khrushchev, reshaping Soviet politics and the dynamics of the Cold War.

events.title: Churchill's 'Iron Curtain' Speech
events.description: Winston Churchill delivered his address at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, declaring that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe, dividing the continent.
events.significance: The speech helped define the emerging Cold War division between the Soviet-dominated East and the Western democracies, and shaped Western policy toward the USSR.

events.title: Birth of Gerardus Mercator
events.description: Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator was born in Rupelmonde, in the County of Flanders. He later developed the Mercator projection, a world map projection published in 1569.
events.significance: The Mercator projection revolutionized navigation by allowing sailors to plot courses as straight lines, and it remains one of the most recognized map projections.

events.title: Che Guevara Photographed by Alberto Korda
events.description: At a memorial service in Havana for victims of the La Coubre explosion, photographer Alberto Korda captured the portrait of Che Guevara known as 'Guerrillero Heroico'.
events.significance: The image became one of the most reproduced photographs in history and a global symbol of revolution and counterculture.
